tagline: You are built for the next horizon and quietly ruined by the ninth one; most of your restlessness is not a search, it is an aversion to being pinned.
overview: Mutable fire is the strangest combination on the wheel: you burn, and you scatter. Jupiter rules you, which makes expansion feel like a moral requirement rather than a personal preference, and it puts you permanently at odds with the idea of a fixed plan. The archer's image is precise if you take it literally — draw, aim, release, and the arrow is in the air before you have an opinion about where it lands. Beginnings are your native element.

It also makes you unusually good company. You can walk into a strange city, a strange field, a strange conversation and treat the strangeness as a gift, which is a rarer thing than it sounds. You also lie more comfortably than most people, to yourself first, and your optimism turns out to be genuinely load-bearing in other people's lives. The trouble is that your promises are so reliable that you skip building the conditions. That gap is where your broken commitments live.

The developmental problem is arrival. You have a strong instinct toward the next thing, and the next thing is always legible in a way the current thing is not, so you keep leaving rooms you have already furnished. Staying, for you, is not a virtue you admire from a distance; it is a skill, and skills can be learned. Saturn eventually transits every sign, and when it reaches yours it arrives with one narrow question: is there anywhere you would stay, if staying were allowed to be happy?
callout_text: You are a lifelong student of everywhere and a stranger to the middle of the sentence.
traits_lede: The generosity and the carelessness are the same faculty. The impulse to widen someone's world is also the impulse to move on once you have widened it, and the two are very difficult to separate.
strengths: Comfort with the unfamiliar — Other customs register as data rather than as something to fear.
Straight talk — You deliver the encouraging thing, even when it is inconvenient.
Real curiosity — You ask questions because you genuinely want the answer.
Contagious optimism — Rooms get lighter when you arrive, usually without any effort on your part.
Long-range instinct — You see which way a thing is heading well before it starts moving.
weaknesses: Promises at speed — You commit while still enjoying the idea of committing.
Bluntness as shortcut — Truth without timing reads as cruelty more often than you know.
Abandons the details — The plan stays vivid; step four is where things quietly fail.
Exits when it deepens — Depth begins to look like obligation, so you call it claustrophobia.
Overcommits enthusiasm — You say yes to the trip, the course, and the idea all at once.
love_lede: You are warm quickly and honest faster, and neither is a small thing to be handed. Trouble arrives when freedom becomes the only condition under which you are willing to stay, which is presumably why the sign is given turquoise: something to carry that is meant to keep the weather from getting to you.
love: You love expansively and in public, which is not a strategy, just how the feeling arrives. You are the one who drags someone across a city to try a specific meal, hands them a book that reorganizes their thinking, and expects gratitude for the disruption. There is a generosity in it that is genuinely rare, and a small impatience underneath: you want them excited now, not eventually. Partners who keep pace with that tend to adore you. Partners who need steadiness tend to call you exhausting, sometimes accurately.

What breaks is not boredom, exactly. It is the moment the relationship becomes the place where the future has already been decided and the only variable left is how you feel about it. You start calling it restlessness. Then you start traveling, harder, with better reasons. The honest version is that you would rather be lonely in motion than settled and known, at least until settling stops being frightening. A partner who reads the restlessness correctly, without demanding you abandon it, can keep you for decades.
friends: You are the friend who makes the trip happen — the one who books it, overbooks it, and comes home with a story and three people you now have to see. Your friendships are warm, wide, and mostly horizontal. Nobody in your circle is a project, and nobody is waiting for you to be their emergency contact. That is a real strength, and also a form of not knowing where you stand, because depth requires staying long enough to change.

When you do commit to one person, you are extraordinary company: funny, honest, generous, and present. The risk is that a wide circle makes it easy to be the one who is leaving rather than the one being left behind. You rarely get left behind. You are usually a step ahead of the ending, and by the time anyone notices, you have already introduced the new person.
career: You need work with a horizon in it — travel, teaching, publishing, trade, diplomacy, medicine, or roles where the job in five years is not recognizably the job in one. Structures that require the same task performed well for a decade sit close to torture, even when you are good at them, which you often are. You are a fast learner inside unfamiliar systems and a poor keeper of boring ones. In practice you are less likely to climb one ladder than to build something with a name and outgrow it.

Jupiter is the great expander and does not distinguish between your income and your ambition. You are generous in both directions: too much spending, too much enthusiasm for projects nobody has costed, and a weakness for backing things that are a good idea and a bad bet. You are most dangerous when a problem gets framed as an opportunity, because you will pursue it past the point of reason to prove something to an imaginary committee. Practical note, from someone with the same problem: a budget and a deadline.
man: You are likable in a way that makes it hard for people to see the ambition, which is the actual thing. You charm first, and it is not an act; it is simply how you meet people quickly. What goes unspoken is that you need the work to be enormous, in meaning and geography, not hours in the day. Partners often assume the enthusiasm is the whole personality. It is not. It is the door you use to get in.

Attached, you are generous, funny, and far too happy to accept blame. You will apologize for something that was not your fault because the mood in the room annoys you more than the accusation does. The failure mode is leaving — emotionally first, physically later — and calling it a need for space, which is usually true and rarely the whole truth. The relationships that hold are the ones where someone can tell you the truth without becoming the reason you go.
woman: You have a reputation for freedom that is partly practice and partly design, and from outside the two are hard to separate. In friendship you are the one who makes things happen. In love you are the one who can talk about almost anything except what you actually need. Jupiter gives you an expansive view of your own possibilities, which is lovely right up until it is used to postpone a decision you have effectively been making for a year.

Your work and your relationships want the same version of you, and that version does not exist. One needs commitment, the other needs room, and you have spent a useful amount of time hoping to give the first one to the second. The interesting version of you is not the one who never settles; it is the one who chose with open eyes and can say why. A relationship survives the choice. It rarely survives the deferral.

faq.a: Sagittarius runs November 22 to December 21 in the tropical zodiac. The boundary is astronomical rather than administrative: the Sun changes sign at a precise moment, often not midnight, so the changeover can fall on the previous or next calendar day. Because the zodiac's reference points drift slightly against the Earth's orbit, that boundary shifts by roughly eighteen hours from one year to the next. Born on November 21 or 22? Check your birth time and exact degree.

faq.q: What is Sagittarius's element and modality?
faq.a: Sagittarius is fire, so it runs on appetite, conviction, and forward motion rather than on feeling or reasoning, and mutable, so it adapts easily and holds nothing permanently. Fire mutable is enthusiasm that keeps changing shape. Jupiter is the ruler, the largest of the traditional planets, associated with expansion, luck, excess, and the urge to make a person into a better version of themselves — occasionally without consulting them first.

faq.q: Who is Sagittarius most compatible with?
faq.a: Aries, Leo, and Pisces are the signs most often described as easy alongside Sagittarius: fire signs who do not need you to slow down, and a water sign who can take your honesty without flinching at it. The harder end is Gemini, your opposite sign, along with Virgo and Taurus — a reliable pattern of friction over detail, pace, and the difference between a plan and a good idea. Easy does not mean harmless, but it does mean less translation.

faq.q: How do I know if I'm really a Sagittarius?
faq.a: Start with the Sun's exact degree instead of the printed dates, since the change happens at a precise moment and the boundary moves about eighteen hours year to year. Then check behavior against adjectives: are you the person who starts things, overcommits, and resents being fenced in? If that reads as a description rather than an insult, Sagittarius fits. If your Moon is Sagittarius, the restlessness is emotional rather than intellectual, which is a different flavor worth knowing about yourself.

faq.q: Why does Sagittarius struggle to stay put?
faq.a: Because the alternative feels like a smaller life, which at twenty-five is reasonable. A Sagittarian's sense of self runs on possibility, and a settled situation quietly stops offering any. This is less a flaw of character than a limitation of design: a mutable fire sign has no built-in mechanism for staying once the novelty is spent. The work is not becoming someone who stays. It is finding something inside a place that keeps producing what you are actually looking for.

faq.q: Why is Gemini the opposite of Sagittarius?
faq.a: They sit six signs apart on the wheel, which makes them a 180-degree axis: two ends of the same conversation. Both are mutable, so both bend easily, and both are quick, verbal, and allergic to being pinned down. The difference is aim. Gemini collects and compares information; Sagittarius wants one large claim to ride toward. Together they are a debate that never closes, which can be wonderful for a week and corrosive by the end of a year.
